page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. Compute capabilities are driven by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz under the x86_64 instruction set architecture. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs paired with 256.0 GB of system memory, establishing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU.

Hardware infrastructure components include a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not bundle local disk storage, necessitating network-attached block volumes for persistent data needs, and it contains no integrated GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Regarding hardware profile efficiency, the configuration prioritizes high memory density per compute core, mitigating resource starvation in applications requiring expansive operational memory. The dedicated core model delivers predictable execution cycles for workloads such as large in-memory key-value stores, distributed memory caches, relational database systems, and extensive data processing pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of memory. This provides an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, matching memory-heavy production profiles. The server features no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for disk operations, and includes no discrete GPU accelerators. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses provided by default. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent computation without hypervisor core contention. With high memory density relative to compute resources, the ecs.r5.8xlarge is suited for memory-bound deployments, such as in-memory databases, enterprise distributed caching, big data analytics, and operational database engines.
